overview: Uraume’s settings tune ice volleys, waves, vortexes, and pillars. Several rows change with cursed-energy level.
technicalOverview: Uraume (CN_250) uses UCN_250_ActionController with nine ordered CharacterUniqueDataTable5 rows: a shared base row, a normal-attack row, three cursed-energy-1 ice-volley level rows, three cursed-energy-2 vortex/pillar level rows, and a super ice-stage row. Character setup resolves each Id_CharacterUnique name to a row pointer in order; the two-hop unique-float helper is an unchecked UniqueRows[RowIndex]->FloatValue[ValueIndex] read. The controller owns persistent fields, crawling waves, trap volleys, pillars, decals, and delayed decals, and its per-frame tick advances all of them on owner time-dilated delta.

CN_250.title: Shared character and ice-wall settings
CN_250.overview: This base row drives the low-HP passive and its healing follow-up, the first normal-attack shot cycle, the crawling wave ease, and three height multipliers for the ice walls raised in the super finisher.

0.label: Passive HP threshold
0.simple: The passive turns on at or below this fraction of maximum health.
0.technical: OnHitPointChanged returns if bPassiveBuffConsumed is true or a CN_250_Passive stack already exists. It then compares NewHitPoint / HitPointMax against this value and adds BUFF_CN_250_PASSIVE only when the ratio is at or below it (the strict early return is Ratio > value). Unitless HP ratio. A generic ProjectionSorceryReceive fallback also reads (0,0) as restraint time only when the incoming damage row is null.

1.label: Passive heal, level 1
1.simple: Level 1 restores this fraction of maximum health.
1.technical: The armed ExtraAttack_1 tick reads (1,0) only when the controller CursedEnergyLevel is 1. It adds HitPointMax * value to current HP, removes CN_250_Passive, and sets bPassiveBuffConsumed. Unitless multiplier of maximum HP.

2.label: Passive heal, level 2
2.simple: Level 2 restores this fraction of maximum health.
2.technical: Same ExtraAttack_1 heal path as index 1, selected when CursedEnergyLevel is 2; HP gain is HitPointMax * value.

3.label: Passive heal, level 3
3.simple: Level 3 restores this fraction of maximum health.
3.technical: Same ExtraAttack_1 heal path as index 1, selected when CursedEnergyLevel is 3; HP gain is HitPointMax * value.

4.label: Charged shot count
4.simple: Controls how many charge shots happen before the final shot.
4.technical: In NormalAttack_1 first-start phase 0, each charge increments ShotCount and sets Phase = (ShotCount < value) ? 1 : 3. With the current value 3, counts 1 through 3 continue the charge cycle and count 4 enters the final phase. Compared as a float count.

5.label: Charge interval
5.simple: Time spent charging before each shot.
5.technical: Phase 0 accumulates DeltaTime and returns while value > ActionElapsedTime; when elapsed reaches or exceeds it, FX_CN_250_01102 is spawned where the charge effect stood and the charge effect is finished. Seconds.

6.label: Repeat wait
6.simple: Wait before a held attack can restart the charge cycle.
6.technical: Phase 1 accumulates time and returns while value > elapsed, then advances to phase 2. Holding NormalAttack_1 in phases 1 or 2 sets bRepeatRequested, which restarts charging in phase 2. Seconds.

7.label: Release wait
7.simple: Wait after releasing before the final shot phase.
7.technical: Phase 2 returns while value > elapsed. If no repeat was requested, reaching this time sets flag 159 and Byte16 and ends the attack phase. Seconds.

8.label: Final shot delay
8.simple: Extra wait before the final shot finishes.
8.technical: Phase 3 accumulates DeltaTime and sets flag 159 and Byte16 once elapsed reaches or exceeds this value. Seconds.

9.label: Wave ease target
9.simple: How large the crawling wave effect grows as it moves.
9.technical: When NormalAttack_2_1 receives a wave order, the wave ease starts at 1.0 and targets this value over 1 second with EaseOut (enum 6). TickWaves advances the ease by 1 / RemainingSteps for each spawned step. Unitless actor scale target.

10.label: Inner ice-wall height scale
10.simple: Final height multiplier for the closest stage-spawned ice wall.
10.technical: The stage trap row with Index 10 (TR_061_00 at 250 units) forwards this value through PlayUniqueAction(200). The ice wall maps id 200 to HeightScale, which multiplies its final actor Z scale and the transform of its finish effect. Unitless multiplier.

11.label: Middle ice-wall height scale
11.simple: Final height multiplier for the middle stage-spawned ice walls.
11.technical: The stage trap row with Index 11 (TR_061_10 at 750 units) forwards this value through PlayUniqueAction(200) into the ice wall HeightScale used for final Z scale and finish-effect transform. Unitless multiplier.

12.label: Outer ice-wall height scale
12.simple: Final height multiplier for the farthest stage-spawned ice walls.
12.technical: The stage trap row with Index 12 (TR_061_10 at 1250 units) forwards this value through PlayUniqueAction(200) into the ice wall HeightScale used for final Z scale and finish-effect transform. Unitless multiplier.

notes.text: The passive is not automatically permanent: the HP hook refuses to start it if the consumed flag is set, and the ExtraAttack_1 heal is the path that removes CN_250_Passive and sets that flag.
The final super stage spawns 18 ice walls. Their distances and angles are hard-coded in the trap-spawn table; only the per-ring HeightScale values come from row 0 indices 10, 11, and 12.

CN_250_NORMALATTACK.title: Normal-attack reach, field, and wave settings
CN_250_NORMALATTACK.overview: This row controls how far normal attacks reach, the persistent field created by the _1_1 follow-up, placement and stepping of crawling waves, and the growth and timing of the NormalAttack_3 spot effects.

0.label: Normal attack reach clamp
0.simple: Maximum horizontal distance used to pull a target or spot toward the owner.
0.technical: NormalAttack_1_1 clamps a chosen field point to this distance from the owner before tracing; NormalAttack_3 uses it as the threshold beyond which a far target is replaced by a point this far in front of the owner. World units, compared against 2-D distance with > and then used as a vector length.

1.label: Field radius
1.simple: Size of the persistent normal-attack field.
1.technical: Passed to StartField as Radius. It sets the FX_CN_250_02102 effect scale (Radius * 0.02) and is later the 3-D distance limit for tracking opponents; opponents with Height >= 0 inside this radius get FX_CN_250_02201 and periodic CN_250_ATTACKB_01_01 hits. World units.

2.label: Field activation delay
2.simple: Wait before the field becomes active.
2.technical: Stored as ActivationDelayRemaining by StartField. TickField subtracts DeltaTime and returns while the remaining value is above 0; only then does it spawn FX_CN_250_02103 and start the fade-in. Seconds.

3.label: Field active duration
3.simple: How long the field keeps hitting opponents.
3.technical: Stored as ActiveTimeRemaining by StartField. In field state 1, after each damage tick the field subtracts DeltaTime and advances to the fade-out state when the remaining value is no longer above 0. Seconds.

4.label: Field damage interval
4.technical: Stored as Field.Interval by StartField. TickField adds DeltaTime to an accumulator and, when it is at or above this value, applies CN_250_ATTACKB_01_01 to every tracked opponent and resets the accumulator. Seconds.

5.label: Charge time and spot trace distance
5.simple: Charge duration for NormalAttack_1 and placement distance for NormalAttack_2_1.
5.technical: Two traced uses share this index. NormalAttack_1 phase 0 waits until ActionElapsedTime reaches this value before firing FX_CN_250_01102. NormalAttack_2_1 also uses it as the forward length of the 60 x 60 capsule trace that chooses the ground spot for a wave. Seconds for the charge; world units for the trace length.

6.label: Wave interval
6.technical: Stored as Wave.Interval when NormalAttack_2_1 orders a wave. TickWaves adds DeltaTime and only attempts a step when Wave.Time is at or above this interval. Seconds.

7.label: Wave step distance
7.simple: How far the crawling wave advances per step.
7.technical: Stored as Wave.Distance; TickWaves traces a wall check and moves Wave.Location along Direction by this distance after each interval. World units.

8.label: Wave step count
8.simple: Maximum number of steps in a crawling wave.
8.technical: Cast to int32 and stored in both RemainingSteps and Unknown40; the wave is removed after this count is exhausted, and Unknown40 also sets the per-step ease rate. Count.

9.label: Spot effect ease target
9.simple: Final scale of the growing NormalAttack_3 spot effects.
9.technical: NormalAttack_3 starts its ease from 0.01 toward this unitless value over row index 12 seconds using Linear easing. The current ease value sets the actor scale of FX_CN_250_05102 and FX_CN_250_05103.

10.label: Far-spot threshold
10.simple: Distance beyond which the attack spot is pulled closer.
10.technical: NormalAttack_3 first chooses the secondary target or target vector. If the 2-D distance from the owner exceeds this value, it replaces the spot with a point this far along the direction from the owner and runs ceiling/wall traces. World units.

11.label: Ceiling lift distance
11.simple: How far upward the attack spot is traced for a ceiling.
11.technical: NormalAttack_3 traces from the chosen spot to Spot + UpVector * this value against ceiling object types; the spot Z becomes the first hit Z or the end Z when no ceiling is found. World units.

12.label: Spot growth duration
12.simple: Time over which the NormalAttack_3 spot effects grow.
12.technical: Passed as the duration of the Linear ease used for FX_CN_250_05102 / 05103 scale. Seconds.

13.label: Final spot wait
13.simple: Delay before the NormalAttack_3 phase ends.
13.technical: Phase 3 accumulates DeltaTime and sets flag 159 and Byte16 when elapsed reaches or exceeds this value. Seconds.

notes.text: Index 5 is deliberately shared by two different normal attacks: the charge-cycle timer and the wave spot trace length; changing it changes both behaviors.

The _1_1 field point is selected by the attack key pressed on the second start (normal 1 = secondary target, normal 2 = nearest teammate, normal 3 = forward) before the row 1 reach and field values are applied.

CN_250_ATTACKG_1.title: Cursed-energy-1 ice volley, level 1
CN_250_ATTACKG_1.overview: Level-1 settings for the ice-wall volley armed when FX_CN_250_07111 plays.

0.label: Attack end delay
0.simple: First-start wait before the cursed-energy attack finishes.
0.technical: The row is chosen dynamically: AttackIndex 1/2/3 maps to this row, otherwise the controller CursedEnergyLevel is used; values outside 1..3 leave the row index at -1. On the first start, TickAttack adds DeltaTime and sets flag 159 and Byte16 once this value is reached; later starts use the normal attack-base tick instead. Seconds.

1.label: Volley interval
1.technical: Passed to StartTrapVolley as Interval. TickTrapVolley accumulates DeltaTime and spawns the next volley only after the accumulator reaches this value; the accumulator resets each volley. Seconds.

2.label: Volley count
2.simple: Number of volleys left before the source effect ends.
2.technical: Passed to StartTrapVolley as the remaining count and cast to int32. TickTrapVolley decrements it each volley and finishes the source effect when it falls below 1. Count.

3.label: First wall delay
3.simple: Pause before the first ice-wall rise.
3.technical: It is put in the threshold list and forwarded as trap action id 3, which the ice wall stores as FirstDelay (seconds before the first rise).

4.label: First wall duration
4.simple: Time taken by the first ice-wall rise.
4.technical: It is put in the threshold list and forwarded as trap action id 2, which the ice wall stores as FirstDuration (the first rise easing time in seconds).

5.label: First wall height
5.simple: Height scale reached by the first ice-wall rise.
5.technical: It is put in the trap volley threshold list and forwarded as trap action id 1, which the ice wall stores as FirstHeight (the first rise target scale).

6.label: Second wall delay
6.simple: Pause before the second ice-wall rise.
6.technical: It is put in the threshold list and forwarded as trap action id 30, which the ice wall stores as SecondDelay (seconds before the second rise).

7.label: Second wall duration
7.simple: Time taken by the second ice-wall rise.
7.technical: It is put in the threshold list and forwarded as trap action id 20, which the ice wall stores as SecondDuration (the second rise easing time in seconds).

8.label: Wall finish delay
8.simple: Wait before the ice wall finishes.
8.technical: It is put in the threshold list and forwarded as trap action id 100, which the ice wall stores as FinishDelay (seconds before the wall finishes).

9.label: Per-wall height scale step
9.simple: Increases the height scale of later walls in a volley.
9.technical: Passed to StartTrapVolley as the volley Unknown08. For wall index i, TickTrapVolley computes Scale = floor((i + 1) / 2) * this value + 1.0 and forwards it as trap action id 200, which the ice wall stores as HeightScale. Unitless increment.

notes.text: The level row is chosen by AttackIndex 1..3, falling back to the controller cursed-energy level; no lookup by attack-set name is used for these floats.
The six threshold values are reordered when forwarded: row floats 5, 4, 3, 7, 6, 8 become trap action ids 1, 2, 3, 20, 30, 100 respectively.

CN_250_ATTACKH_1.title: Cursed-energy-2 vortex and pillars, level 1
CN_250_ATTACKH_1.overview: Level-1 settings for the expanding vortex, its repeating sprays, and the pillars dropped on caught opponents.

0.label: Vortex height
0.simple: How far above the owner the vortex is placed.
0.technical: The row is chosen dynamically: AttackIndex 1/2/3 maps to this row, otherwise the controller CursedEnergyLevel is used; values outside 1..3 leave the row index at -1. On the first start it is the upward trace length from the owner root; the vortex spawns at the trace end or at the first wall impact Z. World units.

1.label: Vortex growth duration
1.simple: Time taken for the vortex radius to expand.
1.technical: Passed as the duration of the Linear ease that grows the radius from index 2 to index 3. Also divides the starting radius in the spray turn-rate expression. Seconds.

2.label: Vortex starting radius
2.simple: Radius at which the vortex begins.
2.technical: Start value of the radius ease and numerator of the spray turn-rate formula. The current eased radius is also used as the spray spawn distance. World units.

3.label: Vortex target radius
3.simple: Final radius of the vortex and pillar capture range.
3.technical: End value of the radius ease and the Niagara Radius parameter. On the second start, an opponent is eligible for a pillar when its 2-D distance from the vortex centre minus twice its capsule radius is at or below this value; the comparison is strictly greater-than to skip. World units.

4.label: Spray turn-rate multiplier
4.simple: Affects how fast the paired sprays rotate around the vortex.
4.technical: TurnRate is computed as index 2 / index 1 * this value * 20. The spray interval is eased radius * PI * 0.1388889 / TurnRate, and the accumulated angle uses 1 / eased radius * TurnRate * DeltaTime. Unitless multiplier inside that traced formula.

5.label: Pillar radius
5.simple: Width and ground-probe radius of a dropped pillar.
5.technical: Passed to StartPillar. It sizes the pillar decal Y/Z, the Niagara Radius parameter, the attack capsule radius, and the radius used for the four ground probes. World units.

6.label: Pillar ground delay
6.simple: Wait before a pillar finds its ground position.
6.technical: Passed as Timer70. TickPillars counts it down, then traces down from Z=1, snaps the base to ground, probes water, sets the sound, and advances the pillar state. Seconds.

7.label: Pillar effect delay
7.simple: Wait before spawning the visible pillar effect.
7.technical: Passed as Timer74. When it reaches zero, TickPillars spawns FX_CN_250_08302_<level>, sets its Niagara Radius and BeamLength, and sizes its capsules. Seconds.

8.label: Pillar finish delay
8.simple: Lifetime before a pillar is cleaned up.
8.technical: Passed as Timer78. TickPillars spawns queued effects while it is above zero; once it reaches zero it finishes the pillar effects, fades the decal, stops the sound, and parks the pillar in state -1. Seconds.

notes.text: Both the out-of-line GetUniqueRow and the inlined variant select rows 5, 6, or 7 from AttackIndex 1..3 with a fallback to the controller cursed-energy level; invalid levels leave the row index at -1.
The pillar level used for FX_CN_250_08302_<level> comes from the controller CursedEnergyLevel captured when StartPillar queues the pillar, not from the unique row itself.

CN_250_ATTACKI.title: Super ice-stage layout and timing
CN_250_ATTACKI.overview: This row defines the super attack decal stage: its total duration, three bands of random marker placement, the ceiling trace and delayed decal timing, the pause before the walls appear, and the finish delay forwarded to those walls.

0.label: Stage duration
0.simple: How long the first decal-spawning phase lasts.
0.technical: StartDecalStage stores it as DecalStage.Duration. TickDecalStage grows the stage decal from 0.01 to 30.0 across this time and advances to phase 1 when stage Time is at or above it. Seconds.

1.label: Marker ceiling trace height
1.simple: How high above a marker the ceiling check reaches.
1.technical: For each randomized marker, TickDecalStage traces from marker + Up to marker + Up * (this value + 50) against ceiling objects. On a hit, the marker Z becomes impact Z - 100; otherwise it becomes the trace end Z. World units.

2.label: Delayed decal effect delay
2.simple: Delay before a marker spawns its ice effect.
2.technical: Passed to AddDelayedDecal as Delay. The delayed decal marker uses it as the EaseOut duration from scale 0.01 to 70; when the delay expires, FX_CN_250_09101 is spawned. Seconds.

3.label: First placement band minimum
3.simple: Closest random distance for the first marker band.
3.technical: Entry 0 Min of the decal stage interval list. Each time the entry fires, FRandRange(Min, Max) chooses the radial distance from the stage centre. World units.

4.label: First placement band maximum
4.simple: Farthest random distance for the first marker band.
4.technical: Entry 0 Max passed to the same FRandRange call for the first marker band. World units.

5.label: First placement interval
5.simple: How often the first marker band fires.
5.technical: Entry 0 Interval. The entry timer starts at 1000 and fires when Time is at or above this value, then resets to 0. Seconds.

6.label: Second placement band minimum
6.simple: Closest random distance for the second marker band.
6.technical: Entry 1 Min used by the second interval entry when it fires. World units.

7.label: Second placement band maximum
7.simple: Farthest random distance for the second marker band.
7.technical: Entry 1 Max used by the second interval entry when it fires. World units.

8.label: Second placement interval
8.simple: How often the second marker band fires.
8.technical: Entry 1 Interval for the second timed placement band. Seconds.

9.label: Third placement band minimum
9.simple: Closest random distance for the third marker band.
9.technical: Entry 2 Min used by the third interval entry when it fires. World units.

10.label: Third placement band maximum
10.simple: Farthest random distance for the third marker band.
10.technical: Entry 2 Max used by the third interval entry when it fires. World units.

11.label: Third placement interval
11.simple: How often the third marker band fires.
11.technical: Entry 2 Interval for the third timed placement band. Seconds.

12.label: Pre-wall pause
12.simple: Wait before the stage starts raising walls.
12.technical: In decal-stage phase 1, stage Time accumulates and advances to phase 2 only when it reaches or exceeds this value. Seconds.

13.label: Stage wall finish delay
13.simple: Wait before a stage-spawned ice wall finishes.
13.technical: Stage trap spawn calls PlayUniqueAction(100, this value). The ice wall maps id 100 to FinishDelay, which counts down before FinishAction. Seconds.

notes.text: The three placement bands are initialized in one block with Time = 1000 so each band can fire immediately on the first qualifying tick; each band independently controls interval, minimum radius, and maximum radius.
Stage wall height does not come from row 8: the trap spawn table Index values 10, 11, and 12 select base-row floats 10, 11, and 12 as the HeightScale argument.
The stage is aborted when no attack action is active, and ResetCharacterSpecificActionState also clears it; the row values only apply while its phase machine is active.

The consumer code is reconstructed: class and member names are ours, but the row and float indices, call order, and branch conditions below are traced from the listed sources. GetOwnerUniqueFloat is only a two-hop accessor and performs no bounds or null checking.

UCN_250_ActionController is created for controller type CN_250 and overrides CreateAction for the character-specific ground and air attack classes; other action types fall through to the shared base factory.

The cursed-energy level rows are selected dynamically by attack index first, not by the attack-set row name: CE_1 reads rows 2/3/4 and CE_2 reads rows 5/6/7. A separate passive heal uses base row indices 1/2/3 by controller level.

The ice-wall forwarding chain is traced through three layers: the CN_250 volley/stage controller supplies FloatParameters, AGameTrapAction_IceWall::UniqueAction stores them by id, and the wall Tick consumes them. This is why several row values appear only as forwarded trap parameters rather than direct reads in CN_250 code.

UCN_250_BehaviorController has no data members; its only specialized behavior branch creates FGameCharacterAIAction_CursedEnergyGuard for AI index 0x16. The AI tick uses the controller field state and the active super action to set think-state values, but does not read these unique floats directly.

Shared MakeUniqueCameraRequest is not assigned to these rows by any traced CN_250 path; it reads floats 0..10 only when an action explicitly calls it with a camera row index. The generic SteerTowardSecondaryTarget reader of base (0,0) is also only called from other character families in the available source.
